proposals.before: He changed his name, disguised himself as a convict laborer, and entered the palace to plaster the privy walls, concealing a dagger on his person with the intention of assassinating Zhao Xiangzi.
proposals.after: He changed his name and surname, disguised himself as a convict laborer, and entered the palace to plaster the privy walls, concealing a dagger on his person with the intention of assassinating Zhao Xiangzi.
proposals.reason: 变名姓 is changing both name and surname; the idiomatic English drops 姓.

proposals.before: Xiangzi heaved a deep sigh, and tears fell from his eyes. "Alas, Yu Rang!" he cried.
proposals.after: Xiangzi heaved a deep sigh, and tears fell from his eyes. "Alas, Yu-zi!" he cried.
proposals.reason: Chinese 豫子 is the honorific Yu-zi, not the personal name 豫讓 rendered as Yu Rang.

proposals.before: Nie Zheng replied, "Han and Wei are not far apart. Now, to assassinate a state's prime minister — a man who is kin to the ruler — this cannot be done with a crowd. With too many people, something will go wrong. If something goes wrong, word will leak out. And if word leaks, all of Han will rise against you as an enemy. Would that not be catastrophic?"
proposals.after: Nie Zheng replied, "Han and Wey are not far apart. Now, to assassinate a state's prime minister — a man who is kin to the ruler — this cannot be done with a crowd. With too many people, something will go wrong. If something goes wrong, word will leak out. And if word leaks, all of Han will rise against you as an enemy. Would that not be catastrophic?"
proposals.reason: Chinese 衛 is the state of Wey, not 魏 (Wei). The idiomatic Wei collapses a distinct polity.

proposals.before: His forebears were originally from Qi but had migrated to Wei. The people of Wei knew him by the name Qingqing.
proposals.after: His forebears were originally from Qi but had migrated to Wei. The people of Wei knew him by the name Qing Qing.
proposals.reason: 慶卿 is the name Qing plus the honorific 卿, not a fused personal name Qingqing.

proposals.before: Afterward, Qin conquered Wei and established the Eastern Commandery, relocating the collateral kinsmen of Duke Yuan of Wei to Ye Wang.
proposals.after: Afterward, Qin attacked Wei and established the Eastern Commandery, relocating the collateral kinsmen of Duke Yuan of Wei to Ye Wang.
proposals.reason: 伐魏 denotes a campaign against Wei, not wholesale conquest; Wei remained a polity whose collateral ducal line was moved to Ye Wang.

proposals.before: Later, Qin conquered Wei, established the Eastern Commandery, and relocated the branch relatives of Duke Yuan of Wei to Ye Wang.
proposals.after: Later, Qin attacked Wei, established the Eastern Commandery, and relocated the branch relatives of Duke Yuan of Wei to Ye Wang.
proposals.reason: Same over-reading of 伐 as conquered rather than attacked.

proposals.before: Once Jing Ke was seated, the Crown Prince left his own seat, bowed his head to the floor, and said, "Master Tian, despite my unworthiness, enabled you to come before me so that I might dare to voice this plan. Surely this is Heaven's way of showing pity on Yan and not forsaking its orphaned people.
proposals.after: Once Jing Ke was seated, the Crown Prince left his own seat, bowed his head to the floor, and said, "Master Tian, not knowing my unworthiness, enabled you to come before me so that I might dare to voice this plan. Surely this is Heaven's way of showing pity on Yan and not forsaking its orphan.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 不知 and renders 孤 as orphaned people; the Chinese says Tian Guang did not know Dan was unworthy, and 孤 is Yan as an orphaned remnant.

proposals.before: Jing Ke pursued the King of Qin, and the king fled around a bronze pillar.
proposals.after: Jing Ke pursued the King of Qin, and the king fled around a pillar.
proposals.reason: The Chinese has only 柱 (pillar); bronze is not in the source and conflicts with 桐柱 in s0307.

proposals.before: Crippled, Jing Ke hurled the dagger at the King of Qin. It missed, striking a bronze pillar instead.
proposals.after: Crippled, Jing Ke hurled the dagger at the King of Qin. It missed, striking a paulownia pillar instead.
proposals.reason: Chinese 桐柱 is a paulownia pillar (桐), not a bronze pillar (銅).

proposals.before: Jing Ke, crippled, hurled his dagger at the King of Qin but missed, striking a bronze pillar instead.
proposals.after: Jing Ke, crippled, hurled his dagger at the King of Qin but missed, striking a paulownia pillar instead.
proposals.reason: Chinese 桐柱 is paulownia, not bronze.

decisions.reason: 变名姓 is the set phrase for assuming a new identity; idiomatic English “changed his name” already covers both given name and surname. Inserting “and surname” is a literal restatement, not the correction of a semantic error.
Xiangzi’s vocative is 豫子, the honorific, not the personal name 豫讓. Rendering it as “Yu Rang” misstates what he cried.
The source is 韓之與衛, the state 衛 (Wey), not 魏. In this chapter 伐魏 later uses the same English “Wei” for a different polity, so the original collapse is a naming error.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 韓之與衛，相去中閒不甚遠

decisions.reason: 衛人謂之慶卿 names him Qing plus the honorific 卿, parallel to 荊卿 in the next sentence. Fusing the two syllables as Qingqing invents a personal name the Chinese does not give.
秦伐魏 is a campaign against Wei, not the extinction of the state. The same sentence still treats 衞元君’s collateral line as relocatable, which “conquered” overstates.
The literal field has the same over-reading: 伐 means attacked, not conquered.

The original drops 不知, turning Tian Guang’s ignorance of Dan’s unworthiness into a concessive “despite,” and it invents “orphaned people” for 其孤. The repair restores both the negation and the singular orphaned remnant.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 田先生不知丹之不肖……不棄其孤也

decisions.reason: 秦王環柱而走 names only a pillar. “Bronze” is not in this sentence and is an invented material detail.
The supplied text is 中桐柱, a paulownia pillar (桐), not a bronze pillar (銅). The original English misreads the graph.
The literal field repeats the same misreading of 桐柱 as bronze rather than paulownia.

claimRevisions.reason: The accepted repair shows that 慶卿 is Qing plus honorific 卿, not the fused English name Qingqing extracted from the bad translation.

value.event: Native of Wei; ancestors from Qi; called Qingqing then Jing Qing in Yan.
Native of Wei; ancestors from Qi; called Qing Qing then Jing Qing in Yan.

claimRevisions.reason: The attestation’s English value copied the fused Qingqing; the underlying 慶卿 / 荊卿 sequence remains valid and is restated as Qing Qing then Jing Qing.
